rationale: A wins because it does the unglamorous work: it tells the founder which doors close if the proof is missing. A's line "Do not pitch this without the harness" is exactly the guardrail this announcement needs; B's "standard launch news" on the first angle is honest, but it leaves one quarter of the set feeling like a warmed-over product note. B is clean and grounded, but A is the more useful strategist in the room.
gaps_in_A: "Two million models, and no easy way to know which ones are safe to use" asserts a safety/provenance gap the update did not give. A partly saves itself by calling it thin, but the headline still overreaches.
"Hugging Face bets the next AI workload never leaves the device" turns one on-device model release into a broad category bet. That needs adoption evidence, not just a laptop/phone runtime claim.
"which ones are safe to use" needs actual evidence about Hub scanning, provenance, malware, licensing, or enterprise buyer concern. Without that, it is a smart suspicion wearing a reporter's hat.
gaps_in_B: "Hugging Face releases a 1.8B-parameter model built to run offline on a phone or laptop" is accurate, but it is the most announcement-shaped angle in either set. A reporter can cover it, but the editor will ask for more than specs.
"standard launch news" is too candid for its own good. If the angle's best defense is that the weights dropped today, it is a weaker story than the business-model, customer, or benchmark frames.
"Next step: journalist-fit-check" skips the live landmine: the benchmark claim is self-reported and unreproduced. Fact-check should come before names if that angle is in play.

"ideally at least one independent reproduction before pitching" is too soft. The set should demand the exact comparison model, evals, settings, harness, and seeds before letting anyone near the performance claim.
